'''Nina Buchmann''' is a German ecologist known for her research on the ecophysiology of plants and on the biosphere-atmosphere greenhouse gas exchange of terrestrial ecosystems. She is a member of the German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina and an elected fellow of the [[American Geophysical Union]]. She was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/</ref>

== Education and career ==
Buchmann has an undergraduate degree in geoecology from the [[University of Bayreuth]] (1989). In 1993 she finished her Ph.D. there working with {{ill|Ernst-Detlief Schulze|de}}<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last1=Grasl|first1=Address ETH Zürich Dep of Environmental Systems Science Prof Dr Nina Buchmann Professur|last2=Switzerl|first2=wissenschaften LFW C. 56 Universitätstrasse 2 8092 Zürich|title=Buchmann, Nina, Prof. Dr. {{!}} ETH Zurich|url=https://usys.ethz.ch/en/people/profile.nina-buchmann.html|access-date=2021-09-14|website=usys.ethz.ch|language=en}}</ref> with a research project tracking the incorporation of inorganic nitrogen into trees.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Wege und Umsetzungen von 15N-Ammonium und 15N-Nitrat in einem Fichtenjungbestand (Picea abies (L.) Karst.)|date=1993|language=German|first=Nina|last=Buchmann|oclc = 722079436}}</ref> Following this, she spent three years at the [[University of Utah]] working with [[James Ehleringer]]. In 1996 she returned to the University of Bayreuth and finished her [[habilitation]] working on the exchange of carbon dioxide between soils and the atmosphere.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Die 13C-Signatur des CO2-Austausches zwischen Boden, Vegetation und Atmosphäre|publisher=[Verlag nicht ermittelbar]|date=1999|place=Erscheinungsort nicht ermittelbar|language=German|first=Nina|last=Buchmann|oclc = 604133058}}</ref> Starting in 1993, she worked at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biogeochemistry]] until she moved to [[ETH Zurich]] in 2003 where she is a full professor.<ref name=":1" /> From 2011 to 2017, she was Founding Chair of the World Food System Centre<ref>{{Cite web |title=Homepage |url=https://worldfoodsystem.ethz.ch/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=World Food System Center |language=en}}</ref> at ETH Zurich, from August 2012 to July 2017 Vice Head of Department and from August 2017 to July 2021 Head of the Department of Environmental Systems Science at ETH Zurich Department of Environmental Systems Science<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-17 |title=Department of Environmental Systems Sciences (D-USYS): Homepage |url=https://usys.ethz.ch/en/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Department of Environmental Systems Science |language=en}}</ref> at ETH Zurich, Switzerland. In the ranking of the “best female scientists in the world” 2024, Nina Buchmann is among the top 6 in Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best Female Scientists in Switzerland 2024 Ranking |url=https://research.com/scientists-rankings/best-female-scientists/ch |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Research.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2007, she was elected into the National Academy of Sciences of Germany (Leopoldina).<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Members |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/list-of-members/member/Member/show/nina-buchmann/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=National Academy of Sciences of Germany (Leopoldina) |language=DE}}</ref> In 2018, she was elected a fellow of the American Geophysical Union who cited "her pioneering work to understand ecophysiological mechanisms regulating ecosystem carbon dynamics locally, regionally and across diverse ecosystems".<ref>{{Cite web |last=AGU |date=2018-11-14 |title=Celebrating the 2018 Class of Fellows |url=https://eos.org/agu-news/celebrating-the-2018-class-of-fellows |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Eos |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2018 and 2019, she was recognized as a "[[Highly Cited Researcher]]".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-13 |title=Highly Cited Researchers {{!}} Clarivate |url=https://clarivate.com/highly-cited-researchers/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=clarivate.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
The main research topics of Nina Buchmann include plant and ecosystem physiology,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kahmen|first1=Ansgar|last2=Renker|first2=Carsten|last3=Unsicker|first3=Sybille B.|last4=Buchmann|first4=Nina|date=2006|title=Niche Complementarity for Nitrogen: An Explanation for the Biodiversity and Ecosystem Functioning Relationship?|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1890/0012-9658%282006%2987%5B1244%3ANCFNAE%5D2.0.CO%3B2|journal=Ecology|language=en|volume=87|issue=5|pages=1244–1255|doi=10.1890/0012-9658(2006)87[1244:NCFNAE]2.0.CO;2|pmid=16761603|issn=1939-9170|url-access=subscription}}</ref> biogeochemistry of terrestrial ecosystems, particularly the response of soil and ecosystem carbon,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Buchmann|first1=Nina|last2=Schulze|first2=Ernst-Detlef|date=1999|title=Net CO 2 and H 2 O fluxes of terrestrial ecosystems|journal=Global Biogeochemical Cycles|language=en|volume=13|issue=3|pages=751–760|doi=10.1029/1999GB900016|bibcode=1999GBioC..13..751B|doi-access=}}</ref> nitrogen and water dynamics to climatic conditions and management regimes and interactions among biodiversity, ecosystem functions/services, and sustainable resource use.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Switzerland |first=ETH Zürich Professur Graslandwissenschaften LFW C. 56 Universitätstrasse 2 8092 Zürich |title=Prof. Dr. Nina Buchmann {{!}} ETH Zurich |url=https://gl.ethz.ch/people/person-detail.nina.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=gl.ethz.ch |language=en}}</ref> She published more than 400 refereed original journal papers<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0826-2980 |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> and 40 books and book chapters (as of 2024), and is member of several Scientific Steering Committees and Advisory Boards.
